evidence.excerpt:
IBM SPSS Statistics (any version) has two issues to resolve before it will run on OS X 10.10: 

1. Download and re-install Apple Java 6

- After the OS upgrade is finished, Apple Java 6 no longer exists on their system. 
- The first time the user runs an application that relies on Java 6, the OS pops up a dialog box stating they've requested Java 6, but none is present.
- The Java dialog has a "More Info" button, which when clicked opens a browser to an Apple Tech Support page for Apple Java 2014-001. A download link is provided (http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572 [http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572]).
- User must click on the download link and a DMG containing the Java 6 installer is downloaded.
- User must open the Java DMG, then double click on the Java installer, follow the prompts and complete the installation.

2. Re-license Statistics

- We use Safenet Sentinel technology for licensing. Safenet writes hidden data somewhere on-disc for keeping track of licensing data.
- The OS X 10.10 upgrade process erases that hidden data. Attempting to run Statistics produces a licensing error and Stats does not start/run properly.
- Solution: Re-run the SPSS License Authorization Wizard, enter auth code again and complete licensing procedure.
- Statistics will now run normally.

result.answer:
*  Scenario for cause of growing QRef entries:
   
    1) The WSDLs have WSPolicy embedded inside the WSDL.
    2) The WSDLs are all local.
    3) The WS Proxy has wsdl-cache-policy & matching is set to "*"
   
   Number 3 is where the problem happens.  Every 30 seconds, the
   WS Proxy is recompiling the locally stored WSDLs and recreating
   all those WSPolicy objects.
   
   
   
   To work around this issue, make one of the following
   suggested changes:
   
    1) Either turn off the unnecessary WSDL cache, or change the
   match expression to something more meaningful, such as
   "http://*" and increase the TTL.
    2) Use the WSDL Status->refresh action to recompile the WSDLs
   which are stored locally.  (Usage:  wsdl-refresh <WSGateway>
   <WSDL>) [S6]

source_lineage.excerpt:
LOCAL FIX
 *  1) Add/remove the WSDL from the WSP Gateway each time you change
   the WSDL.
   2) Add one char to the user summary and then backspace it. The
   apply button will be enabled now.
   3) Add a WSDL Cache Policy.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  The refresh button for the Web Service Proxy exhibited a bug
   such that the "Apply" button would become enabled when "Refresh"
   was pressed. The would allow a customer to apply changes to the
   Web Service Proxy, even if no actual changes were made. This bug
   was fixed, but the customer had grown accustomed to the
   behavior.  This FIN APAR will address this behavior change such
   h that it will be more convenient to address the refresh/reload
   concern.

APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS FIXED IF NEXT.
Check at CLI outputs after executing the show wsm-endpoint command and the objects should be there. If the WSDL is then fixed and refreshed again, the endpoint handler should reappear on the WebGUI.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Following are examples of WSP local endpoint URIs that cannot be used: 

 *  http://.../somename.ns1 
 *  http://.../somename.xsd1 
 *  http://.../somename?ns1 
 *  http://.../somename?xsd1 


This is working as designed in that this syntax is used internally by the DataPower appliance firmware.

APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  A firmware upgrade changes the WSDL option settings such as
   'Schema validate request messages', 'Do not schema validate SOAP
   headers', etc. under the Web Service Proxy Policy.
   
   This only affects the display in the WebGUI. The configuration
   will still work as configured.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  Add the subscription id manually
   through the CLI:
   
   Steps:
   1) co
   2) wsgw <wsp-name>
   4) no user-policy
   3) user-policy "" "" "" "" "" "" <user toggle values>
   <subscription name> on <fragment id>
   4) exit
   
   Subscription name can be found in the WSP Policy Tree and the
   Fragment ID is found under the Web Service Gateway Configuration
   object
   under the "User Policy" tab. Toggle values can be determined by
   running "show" before removing the user policy.

*  Scenario for cause of growing QRef entries:
   
    1) The WSDLs have WSPolicy embedded inside the WSDL.
    2) The WSDLs are all local.
    3) The WS Proxy has wsdl-cache-policy & matching is set to "*"
   
   Number 3 is where the problem happens.  Every 30 seconds, the
   WS Proxy is recompiling the locally stored WSDLs and recreating
   all those WSPolicy objects.
   
   
   
   To work around this issue, make one of the following
   suggested changes:
   
    1) Either turn off the unnecessary WSDL cache, or change the
   match expression to something more meaningful, such as
   "http://*" and increase the TTL.
    2) Use the WSDL Status->refresh action to recompile the WSDLs
   which are stored locally.  (Usage:  wsdl-refresh <WSGateway>
   <WSDL>)

VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID:CVE-2017-1118 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1118]
DESCRIPTION:IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru could allow an attacker to cause the MQIPT to stop responding due to an incorrectly configured security policy.
CVSS Base Score: 3.7
CVSS Temporal Score: Seehttps://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/121156 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/121156]for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L) 

AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru v2.0 on all platforms 

IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru v2.1 on all platforms

REMEDIATION/FIXES
Download and apply the latest version of IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru, 2.1.0.3 from MS81:WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24006386] page.

WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None known [S1]
VULNERABILITY DETAILS
最新の情報については、下記URLの文書（英語）をご参照ください。
Security Bulletin: Non-configured connections could cause denial of service in IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru (CVE-2017-1118 )
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006580 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006580]



CVEID:CVE-2017-1118 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1118]
DESCRIPTION:MQIPT SecurityManagerを使用する場合、MQIPTセキュリティー・ポリシー・ファイルにSocket パーミッションエントリーを追加してIPアドレスが適切に構成されていないと、MQIPTが接続試行に応答できなくなる可能性があります。
CVSS Base Score: 3.7
CVSS Temporal Score: Seehttps://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/121156 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/121156]for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L) AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
この脆弱性は、IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru の下記のバージョンにおいて影響を受けます。 

 * IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru v2.0 (すべてのプラットフォーム) 
 * IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru v2.1 (すべてのプラットフォーム)

REMEDIATION/FIXES
解決策として、下記のリンクからIBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru の最新バージョン(現行 2.1.0.3) をダウンロード、導入してください。 
MS81:WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24006386] [S2]
